title: Async, Threads & Processes
intro: Learn the basic ideas of Async, Threads & Processes in simple English. Read the explanation and example first; the quiz asks only from the concepts taught here.

items.heading: Asynchronous programming
items.text: Async programming lets a program make progress on other tasks while waiting for operations such as network I/O.

items.heading: async def
items.text: async def defines a coroutine function. Calling it creates an awaitable coroutine.

items.heading: await
items.text: await pauses the current coroutine until an awaitable completes, allowing the event loop to run other work.

items.heading: Event loop
items.text: An event loop schedules and runs asynchronous tasks and resumes them when they are ready.

items.heading: gather()
items.text: asyncio.gather() is commonly used to wait for multiple awaitables together.

items.heading: I/O-bound work
items.text: Async concurrency is especially useful when work spends time waiting for network, file or other I/O operations.

items.heading: Thread
items.text: A thread is a path of execution inside a process. Threads can share memory in that process.

items.heading: Process
items.text: A process has its own memory space and can be useful for CPU-heavy work.

items.heading: CPU-bound work
items.text: CPU-heavy tasks may benefit from multiple processes so work can use multiple CPU cores more effectively.

items.heading: Blocking calls
items.text: A blocking operation inside async code can stop other async tasks from making progress until it finishes.

items.heading: Race condition
items.text: A race condition occurs when the result depends on the timing of concurrent access to shared state.

items.heading: Thread safety
items.text: Shared mutable state between threads must be protected or designed carefully to avoid inconsistent results.
